text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today to $140.52, retreating from a peak of $142.28 just two trading days earlier. The pullback comes as crude oil prices have softened slightly—U.S. crude is trading at $89.62 per barrel, down from the levels that likely supported the stock's recent climb. While Middle East tensions (Iran escalating threats as a third U.S. carrier arrived in the Gulf) could normally prop up oil prices, the modest decline suggests those geopolitical concerns haven't been enough to offset other market pressures today.

The broader two-week decline of 4.3% reflects a retreat from earlier strength, though the company remains well above its November 9th low of $134.47. With heating oil prices up sharply year-over-year and crude supply concerns present, the stock's recent volatility appears tied primarily to swings in oil prices themselves rather than company-specific news.
